the following questions: (1) How can sparsity help improve the performance of federated models? (2) How to best exploit sparsity to accelerate on-device FL training? (3) How can sparsified federated models benefit from hardware accelerators?

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we propose ZeroFL, the first framework for efficient training on-device for federated learning with local sparsity.
our framework is the first one to show that sparse training can be efficiently applied to FL and that it is a viable solution for training large-scale models on resource-constrained hardware.
ZeroFL is the first work to introduce and study sparse on-device training in the context of Federated Learning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ZeroFL is a framework that enables training high performing federated models in resource constrained environments by exploiting the sparsity of the models.

ZeroFL is the first framework for sparsifying the training stage of FL, and that we achieve up to 3.4x faster convergence rates and 1.7x lower energy consumption on a mobile device when compared to the state-of-the-art.
we introduce a novel framework that allows to train sparse federated models with up to 95% sparseness and that achieves up to 2% higher accuracy compared with competitive baselines.
The main takeaway from our work is that

sparsity can be a key enabler of efficient on-device training for federated learning, and that a dedicated framework that leverages the unique characteristics of this paradigm is required to obtain the best results.
sparse training can be a key enabler to improve the performance of on-device training in federated learning, while also reducing the memory requirements.
sparse training can be used to efficiently train high-performing models on-device, without compromising the quality of the federated learning system.
